title: The night the lights went out

task.situation: One cold evening in January, there is a power cut in the whole town of Steyr in Upper Austria. Nobody is in danger, but for a few hours there is no light, no TV and no Wi-Fi. Selin, 13, lives in a flat with her mum and her grandpa. Two of their neighbours are Mr Haas from next door and Mrs Okoro from the second floor. Write a story about the family’s special night.
points: what the family was doing when the lights went out
how they spent the evening without electricity

words.short: Write around 150 words. Use the past perfect for things that had happened before.

task.de: Gemeinsame Geschichte über einen Stromausfall in der ganzen Stadt: eine ruhige, schöne Nacht mit Kerzen, Spielen und Nachbar:innen. Erzählt wird in der Vergangenheit, mit Past perfect für das, was schon vorher passiert war. Zuerst wählt ihr, was die Familie gerade macht. Den Titel wählen wir zuletzt.

focus.label: past perfect
focus.note: Marked: every past perfect form (had + past participle), also with just, already or almost and in negatives (hadn’t played). Not marked: past simple forms.

gaps.q: How many hours did the power cut last? Shout a number from 2 to 6.
gaps.qDe: Wie viele Stunden war der Strom weg? Ruft eine Zahl von 2 bis 6.

steps.q: What was the family doing when the lights went out?
steps.de: Hier entscheidet ihr, was die Familie gerade macht, als der Strom ausfällt.

options.label: Cooking dinner
options.teaser: Grandpa is making his famous lentil soup. It is almost ready.

options.label: Watching a film
options.teaser: The whole family is on the sofa, and the film is getting exciting.

options.label: Doing homework
options.teaser: Selin is writing a story for English on her laptop. She is nearly finished.

steps.q: How does our story start? Who? Where? When?
steps.de: Der Anfang stellt die Familie vor und sagt, wo und wann die Geschichte spielt. Lest jede Karte genau, bevor ihr abstimmt.

options.label: Start with the time and place
options.why: Readers know at once who, where and when, and the past perfect shows what had happened before.

map.cook: It was a cold evening in January. In their flat in Steyr, Selin, her mum and her grandpa were in the kitchen. Grandpa’s lentil soup [[had been]] on the stove for an hour.
map.film: It was a cold evening in January. In their flat in Steyr, Selin, her mum and her grandpa were on the sofa. They [[had already watched]] half of a film about a friendly dragon.
map.homework: It was a cold evening in January. In their flat in Steyr, Selin’s mum and grandpa were cooking, and Selin was writing a story on her laptop. She [[had almost finished]] it.

options.label: Start with direct speech
options.why: Direct speech puts us right into the scene, and the family is introduced in the next sentence.

map.cook: “Dinner in ten minutes!” Grandpa called. It was a cold January evening, and Selin and her mum were setting the table in their flat in Steyr. The soup smelt wonderful.
map.film: “This is the best part!” Mum whispered. It was a cold January evening, and Selin, her mum and her grandpa were watching a film in their flat in Steyr.
map.homework: “Only one more page!” Selin said to herself. It was a cold January evening in Steyr. Her mum and her grandpa were cooking, and she was writing a story on her laptop.

steps.q: What happens when the lights go out?
steps.de: Hier fällt der Strom aus, und die Familie merkt, was los ist. Lest jede Karte genau, bevor ihr abstimmt.

options.label: Short sentences
options.why: ‘Suddenly’ and short sentences make the moment exciting.

map.cook: Suddenly, everything went black. The soup stopped bubbling, and the fridge was silent. Selin felt her way to the window. The whole town [[had gone]] dark.
map.film: Suddenly, everything went black. The TV was silent, right in the middle of the best scene. Selin felt her way to the window. The whole town [[had gone]] dark.
map.homework: Suddenly, everything went black. Only her laptop screen was still on, but the Wi-Fi [[had stopped]] working. Selin looked out of the window. The whole town was dark.

options.label: What they heard and saw
options.why: Sounds and pictures help readers to imagine the dark flat and the dark street.

map.cook: At seven o’clock, the kitchen light went out, and the fridge stopped humming. Mum opened the curtains. Every window in the street [[had turned]] black.
map.film: At seven o’clock, the screen went black, and the room went quiet. Mum opened the curtains. Every window in the street [[had turned]] black.
map.homework: At seven o’clock, the desk lamp went out, and the radio in the kitchen stopped. Mum opened the curtains. Every window in the street [[had turned]] black.

options.label: What they saw outside
options.reject: Two mistakes: ‘had went’ (→ had gone: had + past participle) and ‘didn’t had’ (→ didn’t have).
options.rejectDe: Zwei Fehler: Nach had kommt die 3. Form (had gone), und nach didn’t steht die Grundform (didn’t have).
options.text: Suddenly, it was completely dark in the flat. Selin went to the window. The whole town had went dark, and they didn’t had any light at all.

steps.q: How does the family spend the evening?
steps.de: Hier macht die Familie das Beste aus der dunklen Wohnung. Lest jede Karte genau, bevor ihr abstimmt.

options.label: Quiz night
options.reject: That can’t happen: there is no electricity, so the TV doesn’t work. A story must make sense from start to end.
options.rejectDe: Das geht nicht: Ohne Strom läuft kein Fernseher, und eine Geschichte muss zusammenpassen.
options.text: Mum found some candles in a drawer and lit them. Then Selin switched on the TV, and the whole family watched a funny quiz show together. It was a lovely evening.

options.label: An old board game
options.why: The past perfect tells us what had happened earlier: the candles and the old game.
options.text: Mum found some candles that she [[had bought]] for Christmas. Then Grandpa took an old board game out of the cupboard. They [[hadn’t played]] it for years, but soon everybody was laughing.

options.label: Shadow animals
options.why: A small, warm detail: we can see the shadows on the wall.
options.text: Grandpa lit some old candles. In their warm light, Selin made shadow animals on the wall: a rabbit, a dog and an eagle. Mum [[had taught]] her this trick years ago.

steps.q: How do the neighbours join in?
steps.de: Hier kommen die Nachbar:innen dazu. Lest jede Karte genau, bevor ihr abstimmt.

options.label: A visitor from next door
options.why: One visitor brings music, and the evening becomes a small party.
options.text: An hour later, there was a knock at the door. Mr Haas from next door [[had brought]] his guitar and a torch. He played old songs all evening, and everybody sang along.

options.label: Voices on the stairs
options.why: The whole house comes together, and the past perfect explains where the tea came from.
options.text: Later, they heard voices on the stairs. Most of the neighbours [[had come]] out of their flats with candles. Mrs Okoro shared hot tea that she [[had made]] before the power cut.

steps.de: Der Schluss erzählt, wie die besondere Nacht ausgeht. Lest jede Karte genau, bevor ihr abstimmt.

options.label: The lights come back
options.why: The ending goes back to the start of the story and shows what Selin has learnt.

map.cook: After {N} hours, the lights came back on. Grandpa heated up his soup, and they ate it by candlelight anyway. Selin realised that she [[hadn’t looked]] at her phone all evening.
map.film: After {N} hours, the lights came back on, but nobody wanted to finish the film. Selin realised that she [[hadn’t looked]] at her phone all evening.
map.homework: After {N} hours, the lights came back on. Selin’s laptop battery [[had died]] long before, but she didn’t mind. Now she knew exactly how to finish her story.

options.label: Off to bed
options.reject: The task asks how the night ended. A story needs a real ending, not ‘to be continued’.
options.rejectDe: Die Aufgabe fragt, wie die Nacht endet: Eine Geschichte braucht einen echten Schluss, keine Fortsetzung.
options.text: After {N} hours, the lights were still off, and everybody was tired. Selin went to bed with a torch. What happened next? Find out in part two of my story!

options.label: The next morning
options.why: A look back the next morning, with a funny or warm last line.

map.cook: When Selin woke up the next morning, the fridge was humming again. The town [[had been]] dark for {N} hours. For breakfast, Grandpa served his lentil soup. “Best power cut ever!” he laughed.
map.film: When Selin woke up the next morning, the fridge was humming again. The town [[had been]] dark for {N} hours. “Can we have another power cut tonight?” she asked at breakfast.
map.homework: When Selin woke up the next morning, the fridge was humming again. The town [[had been]] dark for {N} hours. At breakfast, she started a new story about a town without electricity.

steps.q: Our story is finished. Which title do we choose?
steps.de: Zum Schluss wählen wir den Titel unserer Geschichte.

options.label: Name the night
options.why: It sounds like the start of a good story and makes readers curious.
options.text: The night the lights went out

options.label: Name the place
options.why: A warm picture and a real place: readers can imagine the town by candlelight.

options.label: A question
options.why: A question with a twinkle: the story shows that a night without electricity can be fun.

checks.en: A title that makes readers curious
The power cut, the evening in the dark and the neighbours are all in the story
The story is told in the past (direct speech can be in the present)
Past perfect for things that had happened before: had + past participle (had gone, had bought)
Everything fits the power cut: no light, no TV, no Wi-Fi
A real ending: the night is over

teacher.aim: Die Klasse schreibt gemeinsam eine ruhige, positive Geschichte über eine Nacht ohne Strom, in der eine Familie und ihre Nachbar:innen zusammenrücken. Dabei üben die Schüler:innen das Past perfect für Vorzeitigkeit (had + 3. Form) neben dem Past simple.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen, Beamer im Vollbild, Hefte bereit. Einsatz ab: Past simple und Past progressive (sicher), Past perfect (had + 3. Form, eingeführt). Optional an die Tafel: go – went – gone, buy – bought – bought, teach – taught – taught. Wörter bei Bedarf erklären: power cut (Stromausfall), stove (Herd), humming (summen), torch (Taschenlampe).
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts) und „Story“ als Überschrift (wie am Beamer), darunter 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen (er kommt zuletzt). Jeder Teil beginnt nach einer Leerzeile, am Rand steht der Name des Teils wie am Beamer: Beginning, Power cut, In the dark, Neighbours, Ending. Am Ende alle Past-perfect-Formen grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext (50 min): 4 min Aufgabe und Heft vorbereiten · 7 Entscheidungen (die erste ist eine reine Wahl: Was macht die Familie gerade?) à ca. 2 min, zusammen ca. 14 min · Abschreiben nach jeder Entscheidung (rund 150 Wörter), zusammen ca. 22 min · 5 min Checkliste und Past-perfect-Formen markieren · 5 min Puffer. Wenn die Zeit knapp wird: Checkliste als Hausübung.
teacher.traps: Power cut C (LSA, Sprachrichtigkeit): „had went“ statt had gone, „didn’t had“ statt didn’t have. In the dark A (CC, Kohärenz und Kohäsion): Widerspruch zum Stromausfall (der Fernseher läuft ohne Strom). Ending B (TA, Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung): kein Schluss („Find out in part two“), die Aufgabe verlangt, wie die Nacht endet.
teacher.notes: Die Geschichte ist ruhig und positiv: Niemand ist in Gefahr, es geht um Kerzen, Spiele und Nachbarschaft. Familie, Nachbar:innen und Wohnung sind frei erfunden; Steyr ist nur der Schauplatz. Die Stundenzahl ruft die Klasse selbst. Nach dem Abschreiben gemeinsam klären, warum jeweils Past perfect steht: Es passierte vor einem anderen Ereignis in der Vergangenheit (Grandpa’s soup had been on the stove for an hour when the lights went out). Differenzierung: Schnelle schreiben einen zusätzlichen Satz mit „because she had …“. Hausübung: zweite Fassung mit einer anderen ersten Wahl (Abendessen, Film oder Hausübung) und einem anderen Schluss.
